reason: I've been coughing up blood for a week and a half.
diagnosis: Active pulmonary tuberculosis is most likely, suggested by hemoptysis, persistent cough, weight loss, night sweats, feverish chills, and recent immigration from India with likely TB exposure and crowded living conditions.
keyPoints: Characterize the hemoptysis: amount, frequency, clots, and associated sputum
TB symptoms: cough duration, fever, night sweats, weight loss, fatigue
Exposure risks: recent travel/immigration from endemic area, close household contacts, crowded living
Ask about TB contacts, prior TB, prior testing or treatment, and BCG vaccination
Screen for alternative hemoptysis causes and red flags: chest pain, dyspnea, smoking, malignancy risk, PE symptoms
Assess infectiousness and isolation needs, including work and household contacts
Check immune status/risk factors such as HIV, steroids, diabetes, or immunosuppression
manner: worried, cautious, mildly anxious, seeks reassurance
transcript:
D: What brings you in here today?
P: Yeah, um, so I have been, I have this cough, I'm coughing up blood so that's made me a little bit worried, um, so I thought I should come and get, get it investigated.
D: OK, yeah no definitely, that, that's definitely concerning, is, so when did this start?
P: It, the coughing up blood started about a week and a half ago.
D: Mhm.
P: Uhm, but it's not getting any better, and it's not stopping.
D: OK and did it start, did the cough just start, uh with, uh, blood in the cough or what, did it just start as a normal cough first?
P: It started off as a normal cough first.
D: OK, and did you have any kind of production of sputum with yellow or greenish material at all?
P: Uh, not really, I mean there, it's, it was a little bit yellow, but now it's just mostly blood.
D: OK and did you have any, did you, were you in contact with anyone that was sick recently, or did you have any travel?
P: I recently immigrated to Canada from India.
D: OK, and were you in contact at all when you were in India with anyone who might have had tuberculosis or was sick at all around you?
P: Uh, I mean it's possible, like people get sick in my family all the time in India, so it's possible.
D: And were you at all, in India when, were you were you living in like close quarters like in a smaller space with other people at all?
P: I have a big family so we all live together.
D: OK.
P: Uh, so it's yeah, so there are about like ten of us.
D: OK great, so it started one, you said around one and a half weeks ago.
P: Yeah, that's right.
D: OK, and is it like a constant cough? Or does it come and go?
P: It's uh, it's pretty constant, well, I guess it comes and goes, it's, it's not there all the time.
D: OK, and have you had this happen before at all?
P: No, never.
D: OK. Right, is there anything that makes your symptoms better or worse?
P: Uhm, I don't think so, nothing that, nothing I've tried has worked.
D: OK, and do you have any other symptoms like a fever or shortness of breath, anything like that?
P: I have been feeling chills and uhm, I haven't actually taken my temperature, but I feel hot, so it's possible that I have a fever.
D: OK, and do you, do you have any significant weight loss at all in the past few weeks?
P: Yeah, now that you mention it, I think I've lost about ten pounds in the past month.
D: OK, and how much do you weigh?
P: Right now I weigh a hundred and ten.
D: OK, so yeah, definitely, that's more than like the ten percent, yes, that is pretty significant. Have you been experiencing any night sweats?
P: Yes, yeah, I've been having night sweats. I thought that was just me being hot, but I guess, I feel chilly and then I have night sweats so I probably do have a fever.
D: OK, and how about fatigue? Are you, do you feel more tired throughout the day?
P: Uh, yeah, I would say so.
D: OK, and do you have any symptoms like chest pain or racing heart or anything like that?
P: No, nothing like that.
D: OK, uhm, any headaches, nausea, vomiting?
P: Uhm, no.
D: Any changes in your bowel movements?
P: uh, nope.
D: OK, any issues with your sleep or appetite?
P: No.
D: OK and, um, any exposures to fumes or dust or animals or pets?
P: No.
D: OK, and uh, currently right now, have you been in contact with anyone else, do you go to work or anyone living with you right now?
P: So I go to work, uhm, I'm working for an assembly line, so there are a lot of people around me and I live with two housemates.
D: OK, and anyone at work or your housemates, anyone showing any similar symptoms at all?
P: No, I don't think so. I haven't asked them, but nothing I've seen.
D: OK, and previously do you have any medical conditions that you were diagnosed with?
P: Nope, I'm healthy otherwise.
D: OK, any allergies?
P: No, no allergies.
D: OK, any kind of loss of taste or smell?
P: Uh, no, nothing like that.
D: OK, are you on any medications at all?
P: Uhm, no, just some vitamins.
D: OK, and any previous hospitalizations or surgeries?
P: Uh, no.
D: OK, other than that, have you had any family history of any heart or lung conditions?
P: Nope, nothing like that.
D: OK, uhm, currently right now, so you live with roommates. Is it like an apartment, is it a home, like a house?
P: I live in an apartment.
D: OK, uhm, do you currently smoke?
P: No.
D: OK, do you drink alcohol?
P: No.
D: Any recreational drugs like marijuana?
P: No.
D: No, OK, alright, so those are all the questions we had. Do you have any questions or concerns?
P: No, what do you think I have and is there anything I need to do right now?
